claim: The current (2026-07-28) MCP specification's own Features section names the three building blocks behind the catalogue as Resources, Prompts and Tools, each with a one-line role; this replaces a prior search-only record whose quote embellished this list with wording ('to gain access to external resource data', 'read only access', 'pre-built instruction templates') the spec does not use.

read: ​ Key Details ​ Base Protocol JSON-RPC message format Stateless, self-contained requests Per-request capability negotiation ​ Features Servers offer any of the following features to clients: Resources: Context and data, for the user or the AI model to use Prompts: Templated messages and workflows for users Tools: Functions for the AI model to execute Clients may offer the following features to servers: Elicitation: Server-initiated requests for additional information from users ​ Additional Utilities Configuration Progress tracking Cancellation Error reporting ​ Extensions Beyond the core protocol, MCP defines optional extensions that add modular, specialized, or experimental functionality.
snippet: Servers offer any of the following features to clients: Resources: Context and data, for the user or the AI model to use Prompts: Templated messages and workflows for users Tools: Functions for the AI model to execute

claim: Descope's comparison piece states MCP's provider-agnostic case in three sentences; a prior search-only record compressed and lightly reworded these into one sentence ('avoids provider lock-in', 'without code changes'), which is close in substance but not verbatim.
query: MCP provider-agnostic universal protocol OpenAI Anthropic no code changes
read: The pain multiplies when your system uses dozens of tools. MCP avoids this problem by being provider-agnostic. It defines a universal protocol for exposing and accessing tools, independent of which LLM you use. The same MCP server can work seamlessly with both OpenAI and Anthropic models, no code changes required. This makes it easy to experiment, switch providers, or even run multiple models side by side without breaking existing integrations.
snippet: MCP avoids this problem by being provider-agnostic. It defines a universal protocol for exposing and accessing tools, independent of which LLM you use. The same MCP server can work seamlessly with both OpenAI and Anthropic models, no code changes required.
title: MCP vs. Function Calling: How They Differ and Which to Use

claim: The specification's own authorization page states, in two adjacent MUST sentences (not one merged sentence), that a remote MCP server acting as an OAuth 2.1 resource server must validate tokens and their intended audience per RFC 8707; a prior search-only record merged the two sentences and stripped the markdown MUST/link markup.
query: MCP authorization resource server OAuth 2.1 token audience RFC 8707
read: ​ Token Handling MCP servers, acting in their role as an OAuth 2.1 resource server, MUST validate access tokens as described in OAuth 2.1 Section 5.2. MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to RFC 8707 Section 2. If validation fails, servers MUST respond according to OAuth 2.1 Section 5.3 error handling requirements. Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive a HTTP 401 response.
snippet: MCP servers, acting in their role as an OAuth 2.1 resource server, MUST validate access tokens as described in OAuth 2.1 Section 5.2. MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to RFC 8707 Section 2.
title: Authorization - Model Context Protocol

claim: WorkOS's spec-update piece states the OAuth-2.1-resource-server requirement predates 2026-07-28 (introduced in 2025-11-25) and that 2026-07-28 tightens it via RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata; a prior search-only record spliced the first and third sentences together and silently dropped the middle sentence that dates the requirement, which matters for a claim about what's newly true.
query: MCP 2026-07-28 OAuth 2.1 resource server Protected Resource Metadata RFC 9728
read: This was introduced in the 2025-11-25 spec but 2026-07-28 tightens it considerably. MCP servers MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) so clients can discover the correct authorization server automatically. MCP clients MUST implement Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) to explicitly specify which MCP server a token is intended for, preventing a malicious server from obtaining tokens meant for a different server.
snippet: This was introduced in the 2025-11-25 spec but 2026-07-28 tightens it considerably. MCP servers MUST implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) so clients can discover the correct authorization server automatically.
title: The biggest MCP spec update ships July 28: What changes for AI agent authentication - WorkOS

claim: The MCP Registry's own about page says only that it is 'currently in preview' with no fixed date and describes itself as the centralized metadata repository providing namespace management and a discovery API; a prior search-only record invented a launch date ('September 8, 2025'), an API-freeze version string ('v0.1'), and a status-as-of date ('July 20, 2026') that do not appear anywhere on this page.
query: MCP Registry preview status server metadata namespace discovery
read:
# The MCP Registry

<Note>
  The MCP Registry is currently in preview. Breaking changes or data resets may occur before general availability. If you encounter any issues, please report them on [GitHub](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/issues).
</Note>

The MCP Registry is the official centralized metadata repository for publicly accessible MCP servers, backed by major trusted contributors to the MCP ecosystem such as Anthropic, GitHub, PulseMCP, and Microsoft.

The MCP Registry provides:

* A single place for server creators to publish metadata about their servers
* Namespace management through DNS verification
* A REST API for MCP clients and aggregators to discover available servers
* Standardized installation and configuration information
snippet: The MCP Registry is currently in preview. Breaking changes or data resets may occur before general availability.
title: The MCP Registry - Model Context Protocol

claim: The specification's own changelog for the current (2026-07-28) revision states the HTTP+SSE transport was deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26, not 2025-06-18 as a prior search-only record (sourced from a third-party blog) claimed.
query: MCP 2026-07-28 changelog HTTP+SSE transport deprecated since which protocol version
read: The deprecated features registry tracks every feature currently in the Deprecated state. Deprecate the Roots, Sampling, and Logging features (SEP-2577). These features remain fully functional during the deprecation window but new implementations should not add support for them. Suggested migrations: pass directories or files via tool parameters, resource URIs, or server configuration instead of Roots; integrate directly with LLM provider APIs instead of Sampling; log to stderr (stdio) or use OpenTelemetry instead of Logging. Reclassify the HTTP+SSE transport (deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26) as Deprecated under the feature lifecycle policy (SEP-2596).
snippet: Reclassify the HTTP+SSE transport (deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26) as Deprecated under the feature lifecycle policy
title: Key Changes - Model Context Protocol

claim: The current (2026-07-28) MCP specification's own authorization page states that authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations, directly contradicting a prior search-only record (sourced from a third-party blog) that claimed 'OAuth 2.1 with PKCE is now mandatory for all remote MCP servers, not optional'.
query: MCP 2026-07-28 authorization OPTIONAL or mandatory for implementations
read: ​ Protocol Requirements Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations. When supported: Implementations using an HTTP-based transport SHOULD conform to this specification. Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment. Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol. ​ Standards Compliance This authorization mechanism is based on established specifications listed below, but implements a selected subset of their features to ensure security and interoperability while maintaining simplicity: OAuth 2.1 IETF DRAFT (draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13) OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Usage (RFC6750) OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC8414) OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol (RFC7591) Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0 (RFC8707) OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC9728) OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Issuer Identification (RFC9207) OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00) OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 OpenID Connect Dynamic Client Registration 1.0 (OpenID Connect Registration) ​ Roles A protected MCP server acts as an OAuth 2.1 resource server, capable of accepting and responding to protected resource requests using access tokens.
snippet: Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations. When supported:
